Veteran trader Peter Brandt has posted an alarming warning about Bitcoin (BTC), suggesting that the world's largest cryptocurrency might never return to its previous all-time high.

In a recent post on X, Brandt shared a weekly Bitcoin chart showing what appears to be a massive head-and-shoulders formation, a technical pattern commonly associated with a bearish trend reversal.

The legendary trader's warning comes amid one of Bitcoin's worst sell-offs this year, with the cryptocurrency losing nearly half of its value since reaching its record high in October 2025.

Sources indicate that brandt's chart reveals Bitcoin forming a left shoulder, a higher peak representing the head, and a lower right shoulder. The cryptocurrency is now testing the neckline of this potential bearish formation, located around the $60,000 to $65,000 region.

Sources indicate that is this a legit H&S top in Bitcoin? If it is I can build a technical narrative that the ATH is in, not to be surpassed at least in my lifetime https://t.co/yoBq2Gp9UK.

A confirmed breakdown below the neckline could indicate that Bitcoin has entered a prolonged bearish trend.

Recent findings suggest that however, Brandt has not declared the pattern complete. His warning remains conditional on whether the formation proves to be a legitimate head-and-shoulders top.

Bitcoin suffered another massive crash on Saturday, Nov. 14, extending the losses that had already shaken the cryptocurrency market earlier in the week. The flagship cryptocurrency plunged to approximately $62,830, with its weekly losses exceeding 16%.

According to recent reports, the downturn accelerated on Nov. 13, when Bitcoin fell below the psychologically notable $70,000 level for the first time since August.

According to recent reports, the selloff was initially triggered by worsening macroeconomic conditions, particularly stronger-than-expected U.S. inflation data that increased expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December.

A stronger U.S. dollar and rising Treasury yields and the Nvidia chaos have also made riskier assets, including cryptocurrencies, less attractive to investors.

On Nov. 10, 2021, Bitcoin reached what was then a historic high of approximately $69,000.

Five years later, the cryptocurrency has fallen below that level.

It has been revealed that for comparison, Bitcoin closed at approximately $65,467 on Nov. 14, 2021. At the $62,830 level shown on Brandt's chart, Bitcoin was trading roughly 4% below its price exactly five years earlier.

Bitcoin's most recent all-time high was recorded on Oct. 6, 2025, when the cryptocurrency surged above $126,000.

That historic rally was supported by strong institutional demand, substantial inflows into U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, and the increasingly crypto-friendly regulatory scene.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, LATEST HAVEN, Conn., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Major global websites, ranging from television networks, common business tools, airlines, and financial institutions are but a few of the hundreds compromised across several industries. If a firm's site was not part of the first wave of attacks, it remains a potential victim.

The attack reveals a systemic, persistent flaw present in nearly every customer-facing website: websites execute code in visitors' browsers, where trusted services can become channels for data theft and transaction manipulation.

It has been revealed that "AI tools have accelerated hackers' ability to rapidly discover flaws in website design and exploit them at scale," stated Ross Hogan, CEO of Source Defense. "Controls are available and can be implemented in mere minutes.".

Source Defense researchers independently confirmed seven distinct variants of the malicious code on sites, furthering research published by Scott Helme on November 16 that linked the campaign to a popular website tool, Optimizely. The code was delivered through compromised Optimizely scripts, illustrating how an attack on a shared provider can expose brands and their visitors without a direct breach of the brands' infrastructure.

Optimizely reports they have fixed the vulnerability, removed the injected code, and implemented additional protections.

It has been revealed that A content security policy (CSP) would not protect against such an attack because Optimizely would be approved even though it's compromised. Permission is based on trusting Optimizely's domain; therefore, the browser will accept a compromised script delivered from that same domain.

The Source Defense Platform for Web Control inoculates websites from these types of attacks by automatically applying granular controls on what website components and scripts are permitted to access, alter, and export.

Recent findings suggest that source Defense's investigation distinguished between the presence of injected code and successful payload delivery. On some examined websites, requests to the malicious domain failed. The presence of campaign-linked code therefore did not, on its own, confirm that the payload executed or data was stolen.

"A website can have strong security around its servers and still lack control over the code running in its visitors' browsers," said Hadar Blutrich, Founder and CTO of Source Defense. "Organizations need that control before the next attack reaches their customers.".

Industry observers note that source Defense Platform for Web Control is a security and data privacy compliance platform for any website that collects sensitive data or is transaction oriented. It addresses a ubiquitous gap in the management of third-party digital supply chain risk with a model that extends security beyond the network to the client-side. Tesorai raises $5.3M to feed starving AI models with biological data and accelerate drug discovery

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Drug researchers and medical laboratories generate massive volumes of biological data every single day, yet somehow the artificial intelligence models designed to speed up drug discovery are still starved of useful information.
  • Industry observers note that it’s a strange paradox, but a startup called Tesorai Inc.
  • The round was led by Perplexity Fund, IQT and South Central Ventures, and saw Latest Stack Ventures, NextGen Venture Partners, f7 Ventures, VitalStage Ventures and ZAKA participating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 18 2026.

Drug researchers and medical laboratories generate massive volumes of biological data every single day, yet somehow the artificial intelligence models designed to speed up drug discovery are still starved of useful information.

Industry observers note that it’s a strange paradox, but a startup called Tesorai Inc. believes it has the solution after raising $5.3 million in seed funding today.

The round was led by Perplexity Fund, IQT and South Central Ventures, and saw Latest Stack Ventures, NextGen Venture Partners, f7 Ventures, VitalStage Ventures and ZAKA participating. With its completion, Tesorai has now raised $8 million in total, and will use that money to try to accelerate AI-driven scientific discovery by digging deeper into existing datasets to surface the deeply buried insights that human researchers have missed.

In a recent development, biological data covers a broad spectrum spanning genetic sequences to protein measurements, and metabolomic processes to cellular imaging. This information is extremely valuable to drug researchers, because it serves as the primary fuel for training advanced AI models that can predict disease pathways and identify upcoming therapies.

AI-accelerated drug discovery is seen as one of the most promising use cases for this technology, but it hasn’t yet managed to change the world in the same way that generative AI has done. Why not? Because researchers still don’t have nearly enough of it, which limits the accuracy of the best models they’ve come up with so far.

It has been revealed that to combat this scarcity of biological data, tech giants including OpenAI Group PBC, Google LLC’s DeepMind, Meta Platforms Inc., Isomorphic Labs Inc. and others are spending billions of dollars to generate more of it, but Tesorai’s co-founders Charlie Kim, Melissa Miao and Peter Cimermancic believe it’s also possible to do more with less.

To that end, Tesorai’s goal is to unlock the biological data that researchers already have access to. Rather than using the summarized findings available in published research papers and clinical studies, it uses AI to analyze raw spectrometry data generated by lab instruments.

Its platform consists of Tesorai Search, which rapidly ingests and analyzes terabytes of data from different sources. There’s also Tesorai Chat, which is used by scientists to ask questions of biological datasets in plain English. And there’s Tesorai Trove, a curated catalog of thousands of publicly available datasets and studies.

Those three components work together to process the raw instrument data from both upcoming and historical lab studies and experiments, before analyzing it thoroughly to try to surface insights that were missed by their authors. By using those insights, Tesorai believes it can train more accurate AI models for drug discovery and therapy research.

“Life science R&D is accelerating and becoming increasingly autonomous, which makes it more important to extract as much insight as possible from every experiment,” Chief Scientific Officer Kim explained. “Tesorai does this for a lab’s latest data and for thousands of published studies, and the gains compound as each experiment builds on the last. Ultimately, this will help the industry to develop better medicines faster.”.

According to recent reports, the startup points to a number of discoveries it has unearthed that were missed by previous studies. In one example, Tesorai reprocessed and re-crunched the data from five studies of the human brain in Alzheimer’s disease-afflicted patients. Through its analysis, it identified a key Alzheimer’s biomarker called p-tau217 that was missed in all five of the studies.

In a recent development, its findings were published in JAMA Neurology in August. In another example, Tesorai illustrated how it was able to accelerate AI model training by adding protein data to a small single-cell AI model, enabling it to beat larger RNA-only models, including one with 40 times more parameters, on multiple benchmarks.

Miao, who’s Tesorai’s chief executive officer, said basically every scientific study produces much more data than what’s reported by its authors. Moreover, most of those studies are never revisited. “Our platform reclaims the value of experiments that have already been done and amplifies each newly introduced experiment with the relevant evidence that already exists,” she said.

In a recent development, tesorai’s early success has paved the way for its initial traction, and it has already established partnerships with the MD Anderson Cancer Center, Fresh York University and the Michael J. Fox Foundation. With the funds from today’s round, it will try to secure more partnerships with the life sciences industry, catalog more public studies and expand its platform to cover other molecular data beyond proteins and genomes.

Sources indicate that perplexity Fund General Partner Joanna Lee Shevelenko stated it’s clear that AI can dramatically accelerate scientific research, and that’s why it needs as much high-quality experimental data as possible. “Tesorai is building the infrastructure to make that data usable at scale, giving scientists and AI systems a stronger foundation for advancing research,” she said.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fitch Ratings revised its outlooks on three major nonbank mortgage companies to negative and warned that elevated leverage and growing mortgage servicing rights (MSR) exposure are weighing on credit profiles in a higher-for-longer rate environment.
  • In a periodic review of nine publicly rated nonbank mortgage firms released Monday, Fitch affirmed all long-term issuer default ratings but shifted the outlooks for Pennymac Financial Services, Planet Financial Group and Freedom Mortgage Holdings to negative from stable.
  • Recent findings suggest that fitch maintained the following long-term issuer default ratings: Onity Group at B-, UWM Holdings Corp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fitch Ratings revised its outlooks on three major nonbank mortgage companies to negative and warned that elevated leverage and growing mortgage servicing rights (MSR) exposure are weighing on credit profiles in a higher-for-longer rate environment.

In a periodic review of nine publicly rated nonbank mortgage firms released Monday, Fitch affirmed all long-term issuer default ratings but shifted the outlooks for Pennymac Financial Services, Planet Financial Group and Freedom Mortgage Holdings to negative from stable.

Recent findings suggest that fitch maintained the following long-term issuer default ratings: Onity Group at B-, UWM Holdings Corp. at B+, Pennymac at BB, Planet at B, CrossCountry Mortgage at BB-, Rocket Companies at BBB-, Freedom at BB-, Finance of America at CCC and Provident Funding Associates at B.

Industry observers note that fitch said profitability for several lenders is likely to be constrained in 2027, given a challenging rate backdrop that limits refinance volume and makes it harder for companies to retain earnings and pay down debt. That dynamic is expected to pressure leverage ratios across the sector.

It has been revealed that at Pennymac, corporate leverage has exceeded Fitch’s 1.5x downgrade trigger since the first quarter of 2026. And a failure to make meaningful progress toward reducing corporate leverage to 1.5x or less over the outlook horizon could lead to a downgrade to BB-, Fitch stated.

“Fitch expects profitability to be constrained in 2027 by a challenging rate environment and the lag in realizing the full impact of recent expense reduction initiatives,” Fitch stated.

According to recent reports, for Planet, the agency pointed to a significant increase in MSR exposure since 2021, as the firm retained servicing from its own originations and acquired bulk portfolios. MSRs represented about 363% of company equity in the second quarter of 2026, up from 293% a year earlier and above the level of higher-rated peers, Fitch said.

Recent findings suggest that planet’s corporate leverage also rose to 5.5x, up from 4.3x during the same period. Fitch considers that level high and a key constraint on the rating. The agency remarked it could downgrade Planet if leverage rises above its 7.0x trigger.

Sources indicate that at Freedom, corporate leverage — measured as gross nonfunding debt to tangible equity — reached Fitch’s 2.0x downgrade trigger in the second quarter, up from 1.9x at the end of 2025. Shareholder distributions exceeded earnings in the first half of the year, contributing to the increase.

Fitch expects Freedom’s leverage to rise further as it grows its servicing portfolio and uses available borrowing capacity to meet potential margin calls under its hedging program.

At UWM, Fitch cited high leverage, MSR valuation risk and reliance on short-term, largely uncommitted secured funding as constraints on its rating. Corporate leverage, excluding origination funding, climbed to 5.3x in the third quarter of 2026, nearly double the 2.7x figure at the end of 2025.

Sources indicate that MSR mark-to-market volatility and a $603 million hedge loss in the second quarter have weighed on profitability. Still, Fitch pointed to a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin for the trailing 12 months through the third quarter as evidence of solid core earnings.

“Fitch expects leverage to decline over time, supported by planned MSR sales and earnings above the expected $165 million annual preferred dividend. Common dividends are suspended. Even so, Fitch expects corporate leverage to remain above 2.0x over the Outlook horizon.”.

Sources indicate that regarding CCM, its acquisition of Two Harbors Investment Corp. brought $156 billion in unpaid principal balance to its servicing portfolio, along with the RoundPoint Mortgage Servicing platform’s in-house capabilities. Fitch expects the added scale and greater retention of servicing economics to improve profitability, although it does not anticipate the full integration benefits until the end of 2028.

Industry observers note that the acquisitions also drove up leverage. Corporate leverage rose to 2.9x, up from 1.2x and above Fitch’s 2.0x rating sensitivity. Fitch expects CCM to reduce leverage toward its 1.0x corporate target. Failure to bring leverage below downgrade triggers within 12 to 24 months could result in a negative rating action.

At Rocket, corporate leverage stood at 1.1x in the third quarter, down from 1.4x at the end of 2025 but above the 0.5x recorded at the end of 2024, before its acquisitions of Redfin and Mr. Cooper Group.

It has been revealed that although Rocket remains above Fitch’s 1.0x downgrade trigger, the agency expects leverage to fall below that level over the next 12 months through repayment of secured borrowings and moderate earnings retention. The pace will depend on market conditions and whether the company realizes the expected acquisition synergies, Fitch stated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prominent market analyst and BitMine Immersion Technologies chairman Tom Lee has offered three potential explanations for the recent crypto market crash that has erased billions in market capitalization over the last few days.

Firstly, Lee points out that the recent crash in AI and semiconductor stocks, especially Nvidia, may have led to margin calls, particularly for retail investors in Asian markets.

According to the analyst, this scenario might have forced investors who needed more liquidity to cover their leveraged positions to sell other assets, including crypto.

Secondly, Lee explains that investors may be selling off their existing equity and crypto holdings to free up funds ahead of Anthropic’s upcoming IPO.

Lastly, the aftermath of the huge $6.3 billion Binance hack that occurred in late October may also be playing a role.

According to Lee, some account holders may be cashing out or converting their recovered funds into stablecoins, further contributing to the sell-off.

Aside from that, Lee has also cited potential risks posed by AI to existing cybersecurity systems and increased U.S. scrutiny of semiconductor sales to Asian markets, including China, as additional factors.

However, these are all just potential explanations rather than confirmed reasons for the downturn.

On Friday, Nov. 13, the world’s largest crypto asset, Bitcoin, fell below the psychological level of $70,000.

Further selling occurred on Saturday as BTC dropped below $66,000 and continued to decline to around $62,112 as of Sunday, its lowest level since July.

As for Ethereum, the losses are even worse, with ETH dropping to around $1,711, its lowest price since early July.

Major crypto assets like XRP and Solana (SOL) are also experiencing massive losses.

With such a sharp decline, there’s been another round of liquidations in the crypto market.

According to CoinGlass data, about $2 billion in leveraged crypto positions have been liquidated in the last 24 hours, with the majority involving bullish traders.

Additionally, this crypto crash has coincided with massive outflows from crypto exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

In a recent development, from Oct. 30 to Nov. 13, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw nearly $3 billion in net outflows, indicating that institutional investors are also selling off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Alan Boyle on Nov 13, 2026 at 2:35 pmNovember 13, 2026 at 2:35 pm.

Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin space venture has decided not to seek further NASA funding for its Orbital Reef space station project in order to tighten its focus on lunar missions.

In a recent development, for the past five years, Blue Origin has played a lead role in Orbital Reef, alongside partners including Sierra Space and Boeing. In late 2021, Blue Origin won a $130 million contract from NASA in the first phase of the space agency’s Commercial Low Earth Orbit Destinations program, or CLD.

Now NASA is seeking proposals for the next phase of the program, which will fund the development of orbital outposts to replace International Space Station in the 2030s. Proposals are due on Dec. 8, with contracts expected to be awarded next spring.

Blue Origin indicated that it will not submit a bid.

According to recent reports, “Blue Origin’s mission is to build a road to space for the benefit of Earth so that millions of people can live and work in space. Establishing a sustained human presence on the moon is a critical step toward that future,” the company mentioned in an emailed statement.

Sources indicate that “As our role supporting NASA’s Artemis and Moon Base missions continues to grow, we’re focusing resources on capabilities that directly advance our lunar projects,” Blue Origin stated. “By sharpening that focus, we can move faster on the technologies and infrastructure needed to make lunar permanence a reality.”.

Orbital Reef was once touted as a “mixed-use business park” in space — and was even slated to star in a sci-fi thriller titled “Helios.” But much like that delayed film project, the space station is now on the back burner.

In a recent development, orbital Reef isn’t the only initiative Blue Origin has put on hold to prioritize moon missions. In January, the firm suspended its suborbital New Shepard program for at least two years for similar reasons.

Blue Origin is building landers for delivering cargo and crews to the lunar surface for NASA. An uncrewed Blue Moon Mark 1 lunar lander is scheduled for launch early next year, and a crew-capable Mark 2 version is scheduled for testing in low Earth orbit next year during NASA’s Artemis 3 mission.

Last week, NASA awarded Blue Origin a $94 million base contract, plus a $140 million option, to deliver a nuclear-powered rover to the lunar south pole. Blue Origin also won a spot in NASA’s broader lunar cargo delivery program. In addition, Honeybee Robotics, a Blue Origin subsidiary, will contribute to a lunar power-generating project known as miniCAST.

Blue Origin is pursuing several other moon development initiatives, including a program called Blue Alchemist that aims to use lunar materials to manufacture solar cells and electrical wire.

In a recent development, several competitors are still working on commercial space stations. Voyager Technologies, Airbus and Northrop Grumman lead the Starlab consortium, which received CLD Phase 1 funding from NASA and is expected to put in a proposal for Phase 2.

In a recent development, axiom Space and Vast are also developing outposts that could take the place of the ISS. Meanwhile, Marysville, Wash.-based Gravitics is building space station hardware for Axiom and an orbital carrier for the U.S. Space Force.

According to the 2026 Holiday Traditions Survey from Mixbook, 62% of Americans who celebrate winter holidays plan to keep every tradition tied to their fondest childhood memories. "What these studies show is that people care deeply about holding on to those moments, but saving a photo is only the beginning. The real value comes when we revisit those memories, share the stories behind them, and pass them on.".

"People aren't short on holiday photos. They're short on time and an easy way to do something meaningful with them," stated Leslie Albertson, Senior Director of Brand at Mixbook. "Hundreds of photos can feel overwhelming, so we're making it simple to find the ones you love and make something you'll actually enjoy and share.".

Industry observers note that the Mixbook app helps people rediscover the photos already on their phones and turn them into photo books, calendars, cards, and shareable Memory Art. With Story Mode, which launched earlier this year, people can start a photo book with a simple conversation about the memory instead of a blank page.

Full results, including state-by-state rankings, are available in the 2026 Holiday Traditions Survey and the 2026 Holiday Photo Report.

The 2026 Holiday Traditions Survey polled more than 2,300 U.S. adults across 46 states in September 2026. All respondents celebrate at least one winter holiday tradition. The 2026 Holiday Photo Report surveyed more than 2,200 U.S. adults across 43 states in October 2026. Respondents primarily use an iPhone and self-reported their 2025 and December 2025 photo counts from the Photos app.

Recent findings suggest that mixbook is a creative photo and memory platform whose photo books have been rated #1 by NYT Wirecutter from 2021 to 2026. Co-founded in 2006 by Andrew Laffoon and Aryk Grosz and based in Redwood City, California, Mixbook helps people turn the photos on their phones into photo books, cards, calendars, home decor, and digital Stories they can relive and share. Over 20 years, Mixbook has earned the trust of more than 6 million customers and over 36,000 five-star reviews.

Loopscale Pauses Protocol After kySOL Collateral Was Priced as zBTC in a 4,597 SOL Loan

📅 07 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1314 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that loopscale's Genesis Vault lent 4,597 SOL against a single kySOL token that the protocol valued as ten zBTC.
  • Industry observers note that one token worth roughly $120 was all a Loopscale vault held when it handed out 4,597 SOL, because the protocol read that token as ten Bitcoin-denominated coins.
  • Recent findings suggest that loopscale, a Solana lending protocol built around Genesis Vaults, paused operations on November 5 after a week of what it called a sustained campaign by a sophisticated actor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Recent findings suggest that loopscale's Genesis Vault lent 4,597 SOL against a single kySOL token that the protocol valued as ten zBTC. The decimal mismatch behind it is the most instructive part of the incident, and a second attack path shows how far the probing went.

Industry observers note that one token worth roughly $120 was all a Loopscale vault held when it handed out 4,597 SOL, because the protocol read that token as ten Bitcoin-denominated coins. The arithmetic behind the mistake is simple.

Recent findings suggest that loopscale, a Solana lending protocol built around Genesis Vaults, paused operations on November 5 after a week of what it called a sustained campaign by a sophisticated actor. Its APIs were taking more than 30,000 malicious requests a day. Loopscale's pause announcement, as summarized on CoinMarketCap, notes user deposits remain secure and affected vaults were restored. The team has not named the suspected attacker.

The loan itself can be traced onchain. A November 1 transaction reveals a wallet Loopscale identified drawing 4,597 SOL after depositing one kySOL, a restaked SOL token. The collateral deposit paired kySOL with a zBTC asset identifier, which backs up Loopscale's account that the collateral was valued as a different asset.

According to recent reports, an independent researcher's trace found that the attacker bought one kySOL for about 1.31 SOL and deposited it into Loopscale roughly 154 seconds later. The protocol priced it as ten zBTC. At the loan's implied SOL price, that kySOL was worth somewhere near $120, while ten zBTC would be worth about ten Bitcoin.

The numbers line up with a decimal mismatch. On Solana, each token's mint account stores its own decimal precision, as Solana's documentation on tokens explains. kySOL uses nine decimals, like SOL, while a Bitcoin-denominated token such as zBTC uses eight. One kySOL is 1,000,000,000 base units, and read at eight decimals, that same raw balance comes out to 10.0. The protocol never had to be fooled about the price of Bitcoin. It only had to read one token's raw amount on another token's decimal scale.

Sources indicate that that arithmetic explains the reported valuation, but it is not a root-cause statement from Loopscale. The team's own description is broader: a misconfigured combination of asset-pricing parameters caused collateral to be valued as a different asset. The result was an undercollateralized loan of about $412,000.

In a recent development, the harder question is how the protocol accepted a mismatch at all. According to the researcher's analysis, the attacker picked a price entry for zBTC, labeled the collateral as an Orca position and deposited kySOL. Under the Orca collateral rule, the kySOL mint was allowed to differ from the zBTC identifier. Labeling it as a standard SPL token would have failed, since that rule demands the mint and identifier match.

According to recent reports, that detail matters more than the decimals. Each rule looked sensible by itself, and the flaw lived in the combination: a price source, a collateral type label and a mint check that together let one token be priced as another. It also explains why Loopscale pointed to both its publicly inspectable program logic and its private transaction-building APIs. Thirty thousand requests a day reads like systematic probing for a combination the normal API would build or authorize.

According to recent reports, loopscale's November 6 update named two attack paths. The second went after the USDC Genesis Vault. Per the protocol, an atomic transaction bundle sold a loan carrying an extreme interest rate into the vault, inflating its net asset value and setting up a disproportionate redemption of about $521,000. Loopscale claims its systems halted that redemption within 30 seconds of the transaction being generated.

So the incident ended in two different outcomes. The SOL path produced a real undercollateralized loan, while the USDC path was an attempt the team claims it stopped. Counting both as stolen would overstate the damage, and Loopscale maintains that depositors took no loss and that affected vaults were made whole.

Industry observers note that loopscale linked four addresses in its disclosure. The two Solana addresses are 247Lk5YNH9URfBBvxVUtDruz8GvGX8gKGuYHVCZThpiR and AzPh2dUV3duK9n8PWV6CxKMwWr9Rk7fxPNBZuv1CiwMr.

The two EVM addresses are 0xb8959Aca4e4C796A3BaDA66833eAe60b1BC0bfb2 and 0xB7Ec7eF24FD73f3000C651CA9D0Fa45b61DcF854. Reports indicate the borrowed SOL was bridged out of the protocol, which fits the pairing of Solana and EVM addresses.

Sources indicate that the loan's later history is visible onchain as well. A November 3 liquidation of the same loan moved about 4,598.4 SOL from a separate wallet back to the lending strategy. The researcher's trace puts the figure at 4,598.434180621 wSOL against 4,597 SOL borrowed, a gap of roughly 1.43 SOL. The liquidator received the lone kySOL as collateral. The public record doesn't yet show who funded that liquidation, so Loopscale's post-mortem will need to explain how the vault was made whole.

Sources indicate that the takeaways are narrow and practical. Decimal scales should come from the token's own mint data rather than a configured identifier, and a deposit should fail when the collateral's mint doesn't match the asset the pricing path assumes. Private transaction-building APIs deserve the same scrutiny as onchain code, because an attacker who can probe them tens of thousands of times a day can map out which combinations they will build.

Sources indicate that vault accounting needs limits too. An extreme interest rate that is legal in the program can still reprice a share if the vault treats the loan mark as authoritative, which is why the 30-second halt on the second path counted for so much.

Industry observers note that this looks less like a clever exploit than a missing sanity check. A deposit worth about $120 should never support a 4,597 SOL loan, and a simple ceiling on collateral value against the borrower's deposited units would have flagged it. Loopscale also lost $5.8 million in April 2025 to a pricing flaw before recovering the funds, so the next thing to watch is whether its post-mortem indicates pricing safeguards that match how often this class of bug has shown up.

Fitch affirms Finance of America’s CCC rating as key risks, leverage persist

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finance of America Companies’ long-term credit ratings remain deep in speculative-grade territory, even as the company reduces near-term risk and improves underlying profitability, according to a review published Monday by Fitch Ratings.
  • Fitch this week affirmed the long-term issuer default ratings of Finance of America Companies and its subsidiaries, Finance of America Equity Capital LLC and Finance of America Funding LLC, with a CCC rating and a positive outlook.
  • Fitch defines CCC ratings as having a very low margin for safety, with default considered a real possibility.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finance of America Companies’ long-term credit ratings remain deep in speculative-grade territory, even as the company reduces near-term risk and improves underlying profitability, according to a review published Monday by Fitch Ratings.

Fitch this week affirmed the long-term issuer default ratings of Finance of America Companies and its subsidiaries, Finance of America Equity Capital LLC and Finance of America Funding LLC, with a CCC rating and a positive outlook. Fitch also affirmed Finance of America Funding’s senior secured debt rating at CCC- with a recovery rating of RR5.

Fitch defines CCC ratings as having a very low margin for safety, with default considered a real possibility. But the ratings agency also explained that it maintains a positive outlook for Finance of America (FOA) due to its “established market position within the reverse mortgage sector,” along with experience senior management and support from Brian Libman, who chairs its board of directors.

In a recent development, the action is part of Fitch’s periodic peer review of nine publicly rated nonbank mortgage companies. Like other lenders, FOA has been contending with volatile interest rates, high leverage and constrained liquidity as the broader mortgage market remains cyclical and capital intensive.

Industry observers note that earlier this month, FOA reported a net loss of $110 million in the third quarter of 2026 as noncash fair value adjustments offset growth in its home equity lending business. The company reported funded loan volume of $748 million from July through September, up 24% from the same period in 2025, while its year-to-date volume of $2.07 billion was up 17% year over year.

The tech giant also noted during its Q3 earnings call that it expects to complete a $60 million paydown of senior secured notes in November. In June 2024, FOA announced a restructuring of unsecured debt into secure notes while extending the original 2025 maturity date. That debt was restructured into two tranches, with $200 million in secured first-lien notes due in 2026 (along with an option to extend to 2027) and $150 million in exchangeable senior first-lien notes due in 2029.

In its report, Fitch stated the positive outlook reflects FOA’s work over the past year to address material near-term obligations and its improved profitability when excluding fair value marks.

The agency indicated it could raise FOA’s issuer default rating to B- if the organization builds a “substantial” liquidity cushion beyond remaining repayment obligations and continues to de-lever through retained earnings.

The ratings remain constrained by relatively weak liquidity and high leverage, a short-term and largely secured funding profile, and elevated key person risk tied to Libman. Additionally, the review factored in the highly cyclical nature of mortgage originations, as well as the volatility tied to mortgage servicing rights valuations and securitization residuals.

The announcement illustrates that while FOA has taken steps to stabilize its balance sheet, its capital structure and earnings volatility still present elevated credit risk for mortgage and capital markets participants — including warehouse lenders and secondary market investors.

Fitch noted that its positive outlook could be revised to stable, or the CCC rating could be cut, if Finance of America fails to bolster its liquidity before upcoming maturities.

Other factors that could drive a downgrade include deteriorating profitability and sustained leverage above 15s. The ratings agency said that FOA’s ratio of total debt to tangible equity — excluding obligations tied to HECM Mortgage-Backed Securities (HMBS) and nonrecourse debt — was 33.7x at the end of September, up from 14.0x at the end of 2025. Fitch said it believes leverage will stay sensitive to interest rate movements.

In a recent development, in December 2025, FOA issued $50 million of preferred stock to funds managed by Blue Owl Capital. Fitch treats these preferred shares as debt, since change-of-control provisions mandate redemption of the preferred shares in cash. But the agency mentioned it does not believe the preferred shares will be a permanent part of FOA’s capital structure as scheduled increases in coupons, starting with a 300-bps increase at the seventh anniversary date, provide an incentive to redeem and create an effective maturity.

“We think it speaks a lot to the interest in the reverse segment, the fact that they’re willing to make an equity commitment to us and acquire the product that we’re generating,” FOA CEO Graham Fleming told HousingWire‘s Reverse Mortgage Daily earlier this year about the transaction.

In a recent development, fitch also noted potential upsides for FOA’s ratings. These include sustained improvement in liquidity after near-term obligations are repaid, return on average assets being maintained above 1% with positive cash generation, and gross leverage staying below 10x.

The agency also cited better funding flexibility through long-term and more committed facilities, growth that strengthens the FOA franchise brand, and deeper management expertise and clear succession planning as potential reasons to bolster the company’s ratings down the road.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 13, 2026 at 3:04 pmNovember 13, 2026 at 7:58 pm.

Updated with officials’ explanation of the cause and the reopening of U.S. airspace.

The nationwide ground stop that halted U.S. commercial air travel Friday was not caused by the Microsoft 365 outage that began a day earlier, federal officials stated at an evening news conference, blaming aging FAA telecom equipment that was overloaded with data.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin opened the news conference by raising the Microsoft outage himself. “I want to make sure everybody understands that there is no connection between this and Microsoft,” he said. “I know a lot of people are making that jump.”.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy likewise ruled out a role for SMART, the FAA’s new AI traffic-planning tool, saying it isn’t connected to the core systems controllers use to track flights.

“There was no possible way SMART would have impacted what happened today,” he mentioned.

In a recent development, the FAA reopened U.S. airspace at 5:15 p.m. Pacific, more than four hours after the problems began, Duffy remarked. He said flights would resume slowly, depending on whether airlines had crews available, and some may not depart until Saturday morning.

Microsoft confirmed in a statement that it had no indication the FAA ground stop was related to its service disruption.

Asked whether a cyberattack or “rogue AI” could be ruled out, Mullin noted there was “nothing completely certain right now,” but “it appears that this was mechanically driven.” He said he could not rule out the possibility of a cyberattack but said there was “zero evidence” of one so far.

In a recent development, what happened: Duffy noted the FAA began seeing unstable radar and communications data at air traffic control facilities across the country at 12:36 p.m. Pacific. Aging switches and routers in the agency’s telecom network “got overloaded with data” and began producing inconsistent information, he said, adding that the FAA still relies on “1980s little copper lines.”.

Duffy noted newer equipment held up.

“Our new IP switches did not go down. It’s the old hardware that went down,” he said. The FAA restored service after deploying fixes to reduce the overloading on its switches, he said.

Sources indicate that mullin noted the overload appeared to have been triggered by newly introduced equipment the FAA was installing. As the agency put “patches into the system” and added “new equipment and new technology,” he said, it “was overwhelming the older system.” Neither official said exactly what that equipment was.

In a recent development, the FAA is in the middle of replacing its legacy telecom network with a modern internet-protocol network. AT&T took over the lead role on that project in August with an initial $74.3 million award, as the FAA works toward a goal of finishing by the end of 2028.

Recent findings suggest that duffy and Mullin used the briefing to press Congress for money to finish rebuilding the air traffic control system. Mullin said President Trump has declared the situation a national emergency.

It has been revealed that the administration has asked Congress for an additional $30.1 billion for aviation infrastructure, AeroTime reported. Duffy said at the evening news conference that he wants $50 billion.

Earlier in the day, Mullin had said officials were looking into a possible link to SMART, including through DHS’s Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA). The FAA said Tuesday it was expanding the system to the airspace managed by all 22 of its en route air traffic control centers.

Industry observers note that the agency describes SMART as a cloud-based system that pulls in about 200 data streams, including weather, flight paths and controller staffing, to recommend flight schedules and routes. FAA specialists review its recommendations, and local facilities decide whether to act on them.

SMART is part of a 12-year, $875 million FAA contract with Boston-based Air Space Intelligence, which denied any connection to the issue. “The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC,” the firm noted.

In a recent development, the FAA halted departures nationwide shortly before 1 p.m. Pacific. More than 3,500 planes were in the air at the time, Duffy said. It’s the second nationwide ground stop since the Sept. 11 attacks, after a January 2023 failure of the FAA’s Notice to Air Missions system.

FlightAware counted nearly 7,000 flights delayed or canceled as of Friday afternoon.

#29796. Done right, verification gives loan officers their time back

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (882 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

Done right, verification gives loan officers their time back

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (882 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Verification has a way of becoming the loan officer’s problem.
  • It has been revealed that A missing pay stub turns into an email.
  • If income, employment and asset verification are handled through separate systems or at different stages of the loan, someone has to keep track of what was completed, what was not and what still needs to happen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Verification has a way of becoming the loan officer’s problem.

It has been revealed that A missing pay stub turns into an email. An employer that doesn’t respond turns into a phone call. A borrower who missed a verification request needs another reminder. And bank statements tend to be the biggest headache of all: pages go missing, borrowers send photos instead of PDFs or the statements don’t cover enough months, so the request goes out again.

If income, employment and asset verification are handled through separate systems or at different stages of the loan, someone has to keep track of what was completed, what was not and what still needs to happen. Even when the underlying problem sits with an employer, vendor or data source, the loan officer is often the one who has to absorb the delay and explain it to the borrower.

It has been revealed that as more lenders move verification earlier in the workflow, often into the point of sale, it is easy to see why LOs might worry that more of that work is being pushed onto them. But moving verification earlier does not have to mean moving more work onto the LO. Done right, it can do the opposite: give loan officers reliable information sooner, reduce manual follow-up and preserve more of the time they need for borrowers, referral partners and newly introduced business.

Loan officers know how promptly administrative work can take over a day. Individual verification tasks may be small, but together they eat into the hours an LO could spend advising borrowers, structuring deals, developing referral relationships and bringing in new business. That is the “green time” loan officers need to protect.

For lenders still relying heavily on manual verification, reducing document collection is one of the clearest places to reclaim time. When borrowers can connect directly to their payroll provider, employer or financial institution, the lender can receive income, employment and asset data without asking the LO to collect every piece manually. That means fewer pay stubs to chase, fewer employer responses to track down and fewer borrower reminders to send.

A direct connection to the borrower’s financial institution also solves much of the pain with bank statements because far less time is spent on things like combing through to identify and source deposits. But automation is only part of the equation. Timing matters, too.

According to recent reports, traditionally, verifications happened after application, once a file reached processing or underwriting. More lenders are now moving those steps to the point of sale, while the borrower is already completing the application. From the LO’s perspective, that can look like more work moving closer to the borrower relationship they manage.

Sources indicate that A well-designed workflow does the opposite. When verification is built into the application experience, the borrower can complete it while already engaged in the process by connecting directly to their accounts instead of manually entering income, employment and asset information in the form fields.

That gives borrowers a faster, simpler application, which makes for happier borrowers, and it gives the LO reliable information sooner without creating another request to initiate or chase later. That earlier visibility also gives the LO more time to address missing information or a financial scenario that needs a closer look before it becomes a downstream surprise.

It has been revealed that moving verification earlier does not help much if the workflow surrounding it is fragmented. When income, employment and assets live with different providers, the resulting data can land in disconnected systems. Loan officers and operations teams may have to toggle between platforms to confirm what’s been completed and rekey information into the loan file.

This fragmentation also creates friction for borrowers, who may not know verifications are the cause, but who will certainly notice they are waiting or being asked for another document. In the worst case, that frustration costs the lender the loan. Even when borrowers stay, verification delays stretch application-to-close timelines, negatively affecting performance metrics that may factor into LO compensation and creating additional costs for the lender.

Sources indicate that A connected verification experience brings income, employment and assets into one borrower flow and syncs the resulting data back to the LOS in real time. That means fewer systems for lending teams to manage, less information to rekey and fewer separate requests for borrowers to complete, helping keep the file moving without adding more work for the LO. Direct-source data can also be refreshed when reverification is needed later in the loan cycle, without sending the borrower back through another round of document collection.

According to recent reports, done right, verification takes administrative work out of the loan officer’s day instead of simply moving it from one stage of the process to another. It gives LOs better information earlier, keeps borrowers moving and protects more of the green time loan officers need to serve customers and grow their businesses.

Loan officers notice which lenders give them verification technology that protects their selling time and which ones expect them to work around operational friction.

  • Monero contributor has opened a pull request that changes how nodes relay transactions coming from Tor and I2P, according to the project's GitHub.
  • The patch addresses a privacy weakness that could allow an observer to connect a transaction to the anonymity network it came from due to the timing of its broadcast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Monero contributor has opened a pull request that changes how nodes relay transactions coming from Tor and I2P, according to the project's GitHub.

The patch addresses a privacy weakness that could allow an observer to connect a transaction to the anonymity network it came from due to the timing of its broadcast.

PR 11743 was opened on November 13 and is at the moment pending review. It is an updated version of a PR opened on November 8 by contributor vtnerd. After receiving feedback from another Monero developer, vtnerd, the PR was updated.

The matter lies in a mechanism where a node receives a transaction over Tor or I2P and then passes it to the regular Monero network.

Currently, when a Monero node receives a transaction over Tor or I2P, it relays that transaction to the rest of the Monero network.

While the transaction is technically private as it travels into the node, once it reaches Monero's public peers, the transaction is no longer private. This PR proposes that Monero nodes will only accept transactions from Tor and I2P peers over incoming connections. Transactions received over outgoing Tor and I2P connections would be ignored.

Recent findings suggest that once accepted, the transaction would be subject to a random delay before being relayed to the rest of the Monero network using Monero's existing transaction relay protocol, Dandelion++. Currently, a user can instruct their node to broadcast their transaction immediately.

Over Tor and I2P connections, this request would be ignored. No transaction would be exempt from the random delay.Being able to link a transaction's timing between the anonymity network and the Monero network is an easy way to deanonymize a user. If a transaction is broadcast to the Monero network immediately after being received from Tor, an observer watching both networks can link the two.

This is a similar concept to a previous PR from vtnerd that would have introduced a randomized delay when relaying transactions from Tor and I2P to the Monero network.

While the amount of code that would need to be modified is not particularly large, this does close a hole for users that rely on Tor and I2P to obscure their location.

When the patch lands in a release is yet to be confirmed. The PR is also labeled for a backport, so it might reach the current release branch as well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 13, 2026 at 4:32 pmNovember 16, 2026 at 10:09 am.

Gov. Bob Ferguson is proposing $10 million to fund basic infrastructure needed for the Northwest Advanced Clean Energy Park, a master-planned industrial area in Eastern Washington that will foster development of large-scale clean energy, advanced manufacturing and supply chains. The proposal will be included in his 2027–29 capital budget.

If approved by lawmakers, the funding would support sewer, water, electrical and road infrastructure at the park.

“This investment will support thousands of good-paying jobs in the trades and advanced industries, and unlock billions in private investment,” Ferguson noted in a statement.

The 1,641-acre site was formerly part of the Hanford Nuclear Reservation, a sprawling federal property along the Columbia River near the Tri-Cities that is undergoing a massive environmental cleanup. Hanford was established during World War II to produce plutonium for the Manhattan Project.

Mel Clark, president and CEO of the CleanTech Alliance, an industry trade group, welcomed the news as the state struggles to get clean power plugged into the grid.

In a recent development, “Washington needs more energy generation, more clean energy, and more manufacturing,” Clark told GeekWire via email. “We’re excited to see the Governor take action to change our last-place ranking in building latest clean energy projects.”.

According to the governor’s office, two projects have committed to locating at the park once infrastructure construction is complete: Atlas Agro’s low-carbon fertilizer production plant and the utility-scale Ruby Flats Solar Farm.

It has been revealed that state officials remarked General Matter is also considering the location for producing advanced nuclear fuel for small reactors. That siting could potentially be beneficial for another project planned for the same area: Amazon, X-energy and Energy Northwest are developing looks for the Cascade Advanced Energy Facility, a nuclear plant comprised of clustered, small reactors.

In 2024, the Norwegian tech giant Cenate expressed interest in building a factory at the park to produce lithium-ion battery components, according to the Tri-Cities Area Journal of Business, ultimately withdrew its plans.

The Tri-Cities is also attracting fusion-energy investment. Last year, Seattle startup Avalanche Energy landed a $10 million grant from the Washington State Department of Commerce’s Green Jobs Grant Program to develop FusionWERX, a commercial-scale testing facility for fusion technologies. The project is being developed in an existing Port of Benton building in Richland.

Washington is heading into its 2027–29 biennial budget with a multibillion-dollar shortfall, but officials have not yet settled on a definitive public estimate.

In a recent development, ferguson has acknowledged the scale of the gap but has not publicly specified an amount. The shortfall concerns the state’s operating budget, which is separate from the capital budget funding proposed for the energy park.
